questions.q: Fill up: Antepartum hemorrhage is any bleeding from or into the genital tract beyond the period of viability or ≥ ______ weeks of pregnancy.
questions.exp: APH is defined as bleeding from/into the genital tract beyond viability or ≥28 weeks. (Book p447)

questions.q: What is the m/c cause of APH and its synonyms?
opts: Abruptio placenta / accidental hemorrhage / uterine apoplexy
questions.exp: Abruptio placenta (accidental hemorrhage, uterine apoplexy) is the m/c cause of APH. (Book p447)

questions.q: Which cause ranks as the 2nd m/c cause of APH?
questions.exp: Placenta previa is the 2nd m/c cause of APH. (Book p447)

questions.q: In vasa previa, whose blood is lost and how does it present?
opts: Fetal blood escaping through the mother's vagina
questions.exp: Vasa previa means fetal blood loss coming out through the mother's vagina. (Book p447)

questions.q: Which listed bleeding is explicitly NOT APH?
questions.exp: Preterm labour 'show' (blood-mixed mucus discharge) is not APH. (Book p447)

questions.q: Uterine rupture as a cause of bleeding is m/c at which time?
questions.exp: Uterine rupture is m/c at the time of labour. (Book p447)

questions.q: A patient presents with APH in the third trimester. Which examination is contraindicated until placenta previa is ruled out?
questions.exp: P/V examination is contraindicated in T3 APH until placenta previa is excluded. (Book p447)

questions.q: Define placenta previa in one line.
opts: Placenta lies in the lower uterine segment
Premature separation of a normally located placenta
Placenta covers the cervix only after 37 weeks
questions.exp: Placenta previa = placenta lying in the lower uterine segment. (Book p447)

questions.q: Define abruptio placenta.
opts: Premature separation of a normally located (upper-segment) placenta
Placenta lying over the internal os
Separation of placenta only after delivery of the fetus
questions.exp: Abruptio = premature separation of a normally located placenta in the upper uterine segment. (Book p447)

questions.q: Sequence of bleeding in placenta previa: uterine contraction/cervical dilation leads to shearing force and then to:
opts: Opening of venous sinuses of the intervillous space
questions.exp: Shearing force opens the venous sinuses (intervillous space); the placenta does not separate and no thromboplastin is released. (Book p447)

questions.q: Which statements are true of bleeding in placenta previa?
opts: Placenta does not separate and no thromboplastin is released
Fetal distress is an early feature
Bleeding is painful and dark red
questions.exp: In PP the placenta does not separate and there is no thromboplastin release. (Book p447)

questions.q: In abruptio placenta, rupture of decidual basalis vessels leads to accumulation of blood, separation and then:
opts: Further bleeding, thromboplastin release and fetal distress
questions.exp: Separation begets further bleeding, thromboplastin release and fetal distress. (Book p447)

questions.q: For a diagnosis of placenta previa, the distance between the placenta and the internal os should be:
questions.exp: PP is defined by a placenta–internal os distance of ≤2 cm. (Book p448)

questions.q: Why should the diagnosis of placenta previa be made only in the third trimester?
opts: Because placental migration occurs with differential growth of the LUS in T3
Because bleeding never occurs before T3
Because the os dilates only in T3
questions.exp: Differential growth of the lower uterine segment in T3 migrates the placenta upwards, so diagnosis is reserved for T3. (Book p448)

questions.q: What are the best weeks for ultrasound assessment of placenta previa?
questions.exp: The best time for USG in PP is 32 weeks and 36 weeks. (Book p448)

questions.q: Thromboplastin release in abruptio placenta causes all EXCEPT:
opts: Tense, tender, rigid uterus and initiation of labour
↑ matrix metalloproteinase → ↑ tissue necrosis → ↑ blood loss
questions.exp: Thromboplastin causes a tense tender rigid uterus, labour initiation, ↑MMP → necrosis → blood loss and DIC – not relaxation. (Book p448)

questions.q: Old classification: Type 1 placenta previa means the placental edge:
opts: Lies within 2 cm of the internal os (lateral PP)
Reaches the margin of the internal os
questions.exp: Type 1 (lateral PP): edge within 2 cm of the internal os, with anterior and posterior subtypes. (Book p448)

questions.q: Type 2 placenta previa is called ______ and its posterior subtype is labelled ______.
opts: Marginal PP; the dangerous variety of PP
questions.exp: Type 2 = marginal PP (edge reaches the os margin); type 2 posterior PP is the dangerous variety. (Book p448)

questions.q: Type 3 placenta previa corresponds to:
opts: Partial covering of the internal os (incomplete PP)
Complete covering of the internal os
Edge within 2 cm of the os
questions.exp: Type 3 = placenta covering the internal os partially (incomplete placenta previa). (Book p448)

questions.q: Type 4 placenta previa is also known as:
questions.exp: Type 4 = placenta covering the internal os completely (complete/central PP). (Book p449)

questions.q: In the NEW classification, 'low lying placenta' equals ______ while 'placenta previa' includes ______.
opts: Type I; Types I, II and III (reaching the os margin or covering it)
Type II; Types III and IV
questions.exp: New classification: low lying = Type I; placenta previa = Types I, II, III when the placenta reaches the os margin or covers it. (Book p449)

questions.q: Match the abruptio variety with its findings: revealed, concealed, mixed.
opts: Revealed – clot (−), bleeding (+); concealed – clot (+), bleeding (−); mixed – clot (+), bleeding (+)
Revealed – clot (+), bleeding (−); concealed – clot (−), bleeding (+); mixed – both (−)
Revealed – both (+); concealed – both (−); mixed – clot (+) only
All three show bleeding with no clot
questions.exp: Revealed: clot −, bleeding +; concealed: clot +, bleeding −; mixed (m/c): clot + and bleeding +. (Book p449)

questions.q: Which abruptio variety is the most common?
questions.exp: The mixed variety is the most common. (Book p449)

questions.q: Page (grade) classification of abruptio: Grade 0 is diagnosed:
opts: Retrospectively, based on the retroplacental clot
questions.exp: Grade 0 is a retrospective diagnosis based on the retroplacental clot. (Book p449)

questions.q: Grade 1 vs Grade 2 abruptio differ in which fetal feature?
opts: Grade 1 – FHS normal; Grade 2 – fetal distress
Grade 1 – fetal death; Grade 2 – FHS normal
questions.exp: Grade 1 has normal FHS; Grade 2 shows fetal distress, both with bleeding + pain. (Book p449)

questions.q: Grade 3 abruptio is characterised by:
opts: Bleeding + pain, maternal shock, +/− DIC and fetal death
Only a retroplacental clot found retrospectively
Bleeding with fetal distress but stable mother
questions.exp: Grade 3 = bleeding + pain, maternal shock, +/− DIC and fetal death. (Book p449)

questions.q: The note lists which risk/predisposing factors for abruptio?
questions.exp: Risk factor is PIH; primigravida and smoking are predisposing. (Book p449)

questions.sec: PP vs abruptio: risk factors & associations
questions.q: The m/c risk factor for placenta previa and its recurrence rate are:
questions.exp: Previous placenta previa is m/c with a 5–8% recurrence rate. (Book p450)

questions.sec: PP vs abruptio: risk factors & associations
questions.q: Which conditions cause a LARGE placenta predisposing to previa?
opts: Diabetes, Rh-negative pregnancy, twins, succenturiate lobe, placenta bilobata
questions.exp: Large placental size from diabetes, Rh-negative pregnancy, twin pregnancy, succenturiate lobe and bilobata predisposes to PP. (Book p450)

questions.sec: PP vs abruptio: risk factors & associations
questions.q: Adhesion formation that prevents placental migration follows:
opts: Previous C-section, uterine surgery or curettage; smoking → endometritis
questions.exp: Adhesions from prior C-section/uterine surgery/curettage and smoking-induced endometritis block migration. (Book p450)

questions.sec: PP vs abruptio: risk factors & associations
questions.q: The m/c risk factor for abruptio placenta and its recurrence rate are:
questions.exp: Previous abruptio placenta is m/c with a 15% recurrence rate. (Book p450)

questions.sec: PP vs abruptio: risk factors & associations
questions.q: Which is NOT a listed abruptio risk factor?
opts: Folic acid deficiency is listed; choose the odd one: young maternal age with first pregnancy
Single umbilical artery with preterm rupture of membranes
questions.exp: Listed risks include folic acid deficiency, ↑ age/parity, smoking/cocaine, thrombophilia, PIH/chronic HTN, fibroid, twins, polyhydramnios, SUA, PROM and trauma – not young first pregnancy. (Book p450)

questions.sec: PP vs abruptio: risk factors & associations
questions.q: Risk factors common to both placenta previa and abruptio are:
opts: Increased maternal age, increased parity and smoking
questions.exp: Common risk factors: ↑ maternal age, ↑ parity (multiparae) and smoking. (Book p450)

questions.sec: PP vs abruptio: risk factors & associations
questions.q: In placenta previa, the m/c malpresentation and m/c lie are:
questions.exp: Malpresentation is m/c with transverse lie more common than breech. (Book p450)

questions.sec: PP vs abruptio: risk factors & associations
questions.q: The m/c cause of transverse lie AT TERM and its management are:
questions.exp: At term the m/c cause of transverse lie is placenta accreta, managed by C-section → hysterectomy. (Book p450)

questions.sec: PP vs abruptio: risk factors & associations
questions.q: Overall (any gestation), the m/c cause of transverse lie is:
questions.exp: Overall m/c cause of transverse lie is preterm delivery; at term it is placenta previa/accreta. (Book p450)

questions.sec: PP vs abruptio: risk factors & associations
questions.q: In posterior varieties of placenta previa, the fetal head pushed into the pelvis produces which sign?
questions.exp: Posterior PP varieties push the head into the pelvis causing Stallworthy sign (fetal distress). (Book p450)

questions.sec: PP vs abruptio: risk factors & associations
questions.q: A bluish, bruised uterus with blood clots in the myometrium in abruptio is called:
questions.exp: Retroplacental bleeding tracking into the myometrium gives the Couvelaire uterus. (Book p450)

questions.sec: PP vs abruptio: risk factors & associations
questions.q: True or false per the notes: Couvelaire uterus is an indication for hysterectomy.
opts: False – it is NOT an indication for hysterectomy
False – but it mandates internal iliac ligation
questions.exp: The notes state Couvelaire uterus is not an indication for hysterectomy. (Book p450)

questions.sec: PP vs abruptio: risk factors & associations
questions.q: Abruptio placenta is associated with increased chances of:
opts: PPH, DIC (d/t thromboplastin) and preterm labour
questions.exp: Associations: ↑ PPH, retroplacental clot, DIC via thromboplastin and preterm labour. (Book p450)

questions.sec: PP vs abruptio: risk factors & associations
questions.q: Name the rare associations of chronic abruption listed.
opts: Chronic abruption oligohydramnios sequence (CAOS) and precipitate labour (<3 hours)
questions.exp: Rare associations: CAOS and precipitate labour (entire labour completed in 3 hours). (Book p450)

questions.q: In a patient of preterm labour with a tense, tender, rigid uterus you should suspect:
questions.exp: A tense, tender, rigid uterus in PTL raises the chance of abruptio placenta. (Book p451)

questions.q: In a PPH patient with sustained fetal distress, which diagnosis must be ruled out?
questions.exp: Sustained fetal distress with PPH mandates ruling out abruptio placenta. (Book p451)

questions.q: Describe the bleeding of placenta previa.
opts: Bright red, recurrent, painless, no precipitating factor; small warning hemorrhage then excess
questions.exp: PP bleeding is bright red, recurrent, painless without precipitating factors, starting as a warning hemorrhage. (Book p451)

questions.q: Describe the bleeding of abruptio placenta.
opts: Dark red, non-recurrent, with abdominal pain and precipitating factors (trauma/PIH/accident), no warning hemorrhage
questions.exp: Abruptio bleeding is dark red, non-recurrent, painful, with precipitating factors and no warning hemorrhage. (Book p451)

questions.q: General examination in abruptio (mixed/concealed varieties) shows shock that:
opts: Does not correspond to the amount of visible blood loss
questions.exp: In mixed and concealed varieties shock does not correspond to visible blood loss. (Book p451)

questions.q: Per-abdominal findings in placenta previa include all EXCEPT:
opts: Fetal parts easily palpable with FHS heard easily
Uterine height corresponding to POG with normal FHS
questions.exp: A tense tender rigid uterus belongs to abruptio; PP gives a soft relaxed non-tender uterus. (Book p451)

questions.q: In abruptio placenta, the uterine height compared with POG and fetal status are:
questions.exp: Height of uterus > POG and fetal distress are features of abruptio. (Book p451)

questions.q: Per vaginal examination in placenta previa is contraindicated because it leads to excessive bleeding. Which other activity is also contraindicated?
questions.exp: Intercourse is also contraindicated in PP. (Book p451)

questions.q: In abruptio placenta, P/V examination is performed:
opts: Only after ruling out placenta previa
questions.exp: P/V is done in abruptio only after excluding PP. (Book p451)

questions.q: Investigation of choice in placenta previa and its purpose:
opts: Transvaginal ultrasound – exact distance between external and internal os
questions.exp: TVS is IOC to measure the exact distance between the external and internal os. (Book p451)

questions.q: Abruptio placenta is diagnosed by:
questions.exp: Abruptio is a clinical diagnosis aided by USG. (Book p451)

questions.q: Screening USG pathway for suspected previa: first ______, and if the placenta is in the LUS then ______.
questions.exp: Suspected PP is screened by transabdominal USG; placenta in LUS prompts TVS. (Book p451)

questions.q: Initial resuscitation for third-trimester bleeding includes which cannulae and investigations?
opts: 2 large-bore IV cannulas No 14/16; ABO/Rh, PT, BT, CT
questions.exp: Resuscitation uses two 14/16 cannulas with ABO/Rh, PT, BT, CT, crystalloids, blood arrangement and catheterisation. (Book p452)

questions.q: Which step is NOT part of the resuscitation checklist for third-trimester bleeding?
questions.exp: The checklist covers cannulas, investigations, crystalloids, blood, catheter, ABC and oxygen – not routine tocolysis. (Book p452)

questions.q: The three assessment parameters after resuscitation are:
opts: Maternal vitals, FHS and evaluation for DIC
questions.exp: Assess vitals, FHS and DIC. (Book p452)

questions.q: If ANY ONE of the assessment parameters is abnormal, the action is:
questions.exp: Any abnormal parameter mandates immediate C-section irrespective of diagnosis. (Book p452)

questions.q: With all three parameters normal, the next step is:
opts: History and P/A examination followed by transabdominal screening USG
questions.exp: All normal → proceed on history and P/A findings to TAS (screening USG). (Book p452)

questions.q: Which triad confirms abruptio on imaging/examination?
opts: Placenta in upper uterine segment, retroplacental clot, Jello sign positive
Placenta in LUS, snowstorm, theca lutein cysts
questions.exp: Abruptio (+): placenta in UUS, retroplacental clot and Jello sign (shimmering placenta on movement). (Book p452)

questions.q: The Jello sign refers to:
opts: Shimmering of the placenta on movement
questions.exp: Jello sign = shimmering of the placenta on movement, seen in abruptio. (Book p452)

questions.q: A placenta found in the LUS in T1/T2 without any history of P/V bleeding will migrate in what proportion of cases?
questions.exp: In 80–90% of such cases placental migration occurs. (Book p452)

questions.q: Advice given to a patient with a low-lying placenta includes avoiding:
opts: Intercourse, physical exercise, heavy lifting and standing ≥4 hours
questions.exp: Avoid intercourse, exercise, heavy weights and standing ≥4 hours; TVS at 32 weeks and report any bleeding. (Book p453)

questions.q: Follow-up scan schedule: no P/V bleeding → repeat USG at 32 weeks; if placenta still in LUS →
questions.exp: Placenta in LUS at 32 weeks → repeat TVS at 36 weeks. (Book p453)

questions.q: If the placenta is STILL in the LUS at 36 weeks, delivery is planned as:
questions.exp: Persistent LUS placenta → plan C-section between 36–37 weeks + 6 days. (Book p453)

questions.q: If at follow-up the placenta is in the upper uterine segment, the interpretation is:
opts: Migration has occurred – not a case of placenta previa
questions.exp: Placenta in UUS means migration occurred; it is not placenta previa. (Book p453)

questions.q: Mode of delivery: a low-lying placenta 1–2 cm from the internal os is best managed by:
opts: C-section preferred, though vaginal delivery can be done
questions.exp: Between 1–2 cm of the internal os, C-section is preferred but vaginal delivery is possible. (Book p453)

questions.q: A placenta within 1 cm of the internal os, and true placenta previa, require:
questions.exp: Within 1 cm → C-section; placenta previa → always C-section. (Book p453)

questions.q: In placenta previa WITH active bleeding, expectant management aims to:
opts: Continue pregnancy to attain fetal lung maturity without risking the mother's life
questions.exp: Expectant care continues pregnancy for fetal lung maturity without risking maternal life; active management terminates immediately by C-section. (Book p453)

questions.q: Which combination favours EXPECTANT management of bleeding previa?
opts: Stable vitals, absent active bleeding, <37 weeks, reactive CTG, no/minor anomaly – ALL conditions present
Gross congenital anomaly of a non-viable fetus
questions.exp: Expectant needs ALL of: stable vitals, no active bleeding, <37 weeks, normal FHS/CTG and no major anomaly. (Book p454)

questions.q: Which single finding triggers ACTIVE management in bleeding previa?
questions.exp: ANY one of unstable vitals, active bleeding, ≥37 weeks (or ≥34 weeks with extreme loss), fetal distress or gross anomaly triggers active management. (Book p454)

questions.q: At what gestation does active management become indicated even without extreme blood loss?
questions.exp: POG ≥37 weeks favours active management; ≥34 weeks only with extreme blood loss. (Book p454)

questions.q: Expectant management of previa is also named the ______ regime and starts with:
opts: MacAfee/Johnson's regime – admit the patient with bed rest
questions.exp: Expectant management = MacAfee/Johnson's regime beginning with admission and bed rest. (Book p454)

questions.q: Monitoring during expectant management covers:
opts: Maternal vitals, FHS and bleeding, with blood arranged
questions.exp: Monitor maternal vitals, FHS and bleeding; arrange blood; give anti-D if Rh-negative. (Book p454)

questions.q: An Rh-negative mother under expectant management should receive:
questions.exp: Anti-D is given if the patient is Rh-negative. (Book p454)

questions.q: Steroid and tocolytic rules in expectant previa: POG <34 weeks gets ______ and POG <32 weeks adds ______.
opts: Dexamethasone + tocolytics; MgSO4 for neural protection
questions.exp: <34 weeks: dexamethasone + tocolytics; <32 weeks: add MgSO4 for fetal neural protection; continue till 37 weeks then elective C-section (36–37 weeks). (Book p454)

questions.q: In ALL cases of placenta previa the notes advise suspecting:
questions.exp: Every previa should raise suspicion of placenta accreta. (Book p454)

questions.q: If Doppler USG in previa shows accreta features, the operative plan becomes:
questions.exp: With accreta present, C-section proceeds to hysterectomy (caesarean hysterectomy). (Book p454)

questions.q: An abruptio patient presenting in labour pain with maternal vitals unstable, fetal distress, DIC or acute kidney injury needs:
questions.exp: These emergency conditions mandate immediate C-section. (Book p455)

questions.q: In abruptio with FETAL DEATH, vaginal delivery is acceptable when:
opts: Maternal vitals are stable and there is no DIC
questions.exp: Fetal death with stable mother and no DIC allows vaginal delivery; instability or DIC pushes to C-section. (Book p455)

questions.q: A non-emergency abruptio (normal FHS) at ≥34 weeks is managed by:
opts: Induction of labour for vaginal delivery
questions.exp: ≥34 weeks → induction of labour/vaginal delivery; <34 weeks → expectant management. (Book p455)

questions.q: DIC is also called ______ and includes which obstetric causes?
opts: Consumptive coagulopathy; abruptio, amniotic fluid embolism, septic abortion, acute fatty liver, IUD ≥4 weeks, rarely severe PE/eclampsia/HELLP
questions.exp: DIC = consumptive coagulopathy with the listed obstetric causes including IUD retained ≥4 weeks. (Book p455)

questions.q: Management of DIC includes:
questions.exp: Treat DIC with cryoprecipitate, FFP and blood transfusion. (Book p455)

questions.q: In abruptio WITH DIC, the first step is:
questions.exp: In abruptio + DIC, manage DIC first and then proceed to C-section. (Book p455)

questions.q: Differential diagnosis of bleeding beyond 28 weeks includes all EXCEPT:
opts: Cervical ectropion bleed as a listed APH cause
questions.exp: The D/D list is APH (abruptio, previa, vasa previa), preterm labour show and uterine rupture. (Book p456)

questions.q: Labour vs abruptio: match P/V, cervix and fetus findings.
opts: Labour – blood-mixed mucus discharge, progressive cervical dilatation, FHS normal; abruptio – bleeding, no progressive dilatation, fetal distress
Labour – frank bleeding, no dilatation, distress; abruptio – show, dilatation, normal FHS
questions.exp: Labour shows mucus-discharge, progressive dilatation and normal FHS; abruptio shows bleeding and fetal distress. (Book p456)

questions.q: If the distinction between labour and abruptio is doubtful, the next step is:
questions.exp: When doubtful, ARM is performed to inspect the liquor. (Book p456)

questions.q: ARM in abruptio yields which liquor and effects?
opts: Dark red liquor; accelerates labour; increases bleeding
Meconium-stained liquor; no effect on labour
questions.exp: In abruptio ARM shows dark red liquor, accelerates labour and ↑ bleeding. (Book p456)

questions.q: Abruptio vs ruptured uterus: which history and P/A pair belongs to ruptured uterus?
opts: H/o previous LSCS; uterine contour not felt with fetal parts felt superficially in the peritoneal cavity
H/o trauma/PIH; tender rigid uterus with fundal height > POG
H/o trauma; fetal parts not palpable
H/o PIH; loss of fetal station on P/A
questions.exp: Ruptured uterus follows previous LSCS with loss of uterine contour and superficially felt parts; P/V shows loss of fetal station. (Book p456)

questions.q: On P/V examination, loss of fetal station suggests:
questions.exp: Loss of fetal station on P/V is the ruptured-uterus counterpart to a palpable head in abruptio. (Book p456)

questions.q: Placenta accreta spectrum was previously known as:
questions.exp: PAS was previously called morbidly adherent placenta. (Book p457)

questions.q: FIGO grade 1 of PAS describes:
opts: Placenta accreta – villi superficially attached to myometrium (m/c)
questions.exp: Grade 1 = accreta with superficial myometrial attachment, the m/c grade. (Book p457)

questions.q: Match: grade 2 and grade 3 PAS.
opts: Grade 2 increta – villi infiltrate into myometrium; grade 3 percreta – villi attached to serosa (3a serosa, 3b bladder, 3c other pelvic structures)
questions.exp: Increta infiltrates the myometrium; percreta reaches serosa (3a), bladder (3b) or other pelvic structures (3c). (Book p457)

questions.q: The three etiopathogenic mechanisms of PAS are:
opts: Absent decidua basalis/defective decidualization, absent Nitabuch's layer, hyper-invasiveness of cytotrophoblast
questions.exp: PAS arises from deficient decidua/Nitabuch's layer and hyper-invasive cytotrophoblast. (Book p457)

questions.q: Nitabuch's layer is a layer of fibrinoid degeneration between ______ and its function is to:
opts: Trophoblast and decidua basalis; limit villous penetration into decidua
questions.exp: Nitabuch's layer lies between trophoblast and decidua basalis and limits penetration; its absence allows deeper invasion. (Book p457)

questions.q: The foremost risk factor for PAS in the current pregnancy is:
questions.exp: Anterior placenta previa in the present pregnancy heads the risk list. (Book p458)

questions.q: Previous surgeries predisposing to PAS include:
opts: C-section, myomectomy, curettage and endometrial ablation
questions.exp: Prior C-section (risk ↑ with number), myomectomy, curettage and endometrial ablation predispose to PAS. (Book p458)

questions.q: Maternal serum markers (not done routinely) that raise PAS risk are:
questions.exp: Maternal serum AFP ≥2.5 MoM and hCG ≥2.5 MoM indicate ↑ PAS risk. (Book p458)

questions.q: Screening and definitive diagnosis of PAS are:
opts: Anomaly scan (findings in T2); USG with colour Doppler (IOC) at 28 weeks
First-trimester NT scan; MRI at 12 weeks
questions.exp: Screening is the anomaly scan with characteristic T2 findings; definitive is colour Doppler USG (IOC) at 28 weeks. (Book p458)

questions.q: Which USG sign of PAS describes sonolucent areas with a moth-eaten appearance and ↑ vascularity on Doppler?
questions.exp: Large lacunae/lakes with moth-eaten appearance and hypervascular lacunae are PAS signs. (Book p458)

questions.q: Thinning of the retroplacental myometrium in PAS is defined as a serosa–myometrium distance of:
questions.exp: A distance <1 mm between serosa and myometrium defines thinning. (Book p458)

questions.q: Bridging vessels in PAS are seen between the placenta and:
questions.exp: Bridging vessels cross the placenta–bladder/serosa interface with Doppler hypervascularity. (Book p458)

questions.q: Two further USG signs of PAS listed are disruption of the continuous white line and:
opts: Loss of the normal retroplacental hypoechoic area (decidua basalis)
questions.exp: Loss of the retroplacental hypoechoic area (decidua basalis) and white-line disruption support PAS. (Book p458)

questions.q: MRI in PAS workup is reserved for:
opts: Cases where USG + Doppler are inconclusive
questions.exp: MRI is used only when USG with Doppler is inconclusive. (Book p458)

questions.q: ACOG's management of choice for antenatally detected PAS is:
opts: Elective C-section between 34–35 weeks + 6/7 days followed by hysterectomy with placenta in situ
C-section at 39 weeks with placental removal
questions.exp: ACOG: elective C-section at 34–35 weeks + 6/7 days then hysterectomy leaving the placenta in situ. (Book p459)

questions.q: During caesarean hysterectomy for PAS, which anaesthesia and incision are preferred?
opts: General anaesthesia with classical C-section avoiding the placental site
Spinal anaesthesia with low transverse incision through the placenta
Local anaesthesia with vertical skin incision
General anaesthesia with incision through the placental site
questions.exp: GA is preferred and a classical C-section avoids the placental site. (Book p459)

questions.q: Two intraoperative rules for PAS caesarean hysterectomy are:
opts: No attempt to separate/deliver the placenta and close the uterine incision before hysterectomy
Deliver the placenta manually then hysterectomy
Leave the uterus open during hysterectomy
Separate the placenta with cord traction
questions.exp: The placenta is left undisturbed and the uterine incision is closed prior to hysterectomy to avoid bleeding. (Book p459)

questions.q: Pre-operative ureteric catheterization in PAS offers which advantage and limitation?
opts: Helps ureteric identification if bladder invasion exists; does NOT reduce urinary tract injury risk
Prevents all ureteric injury; no advantage in identification
Guides bladder repair; contraindicated in percreta
questions.exp: It aids identification but does not lower urinary tract injury risk. (Book p459)

questions.q: Pre-operative internal iliac artery balloon catheters are inflated post-delivery to reduce pelvic blood flow. Why does ACOG NOT recommend them?
questions.exp: The ↑ embolization risk makes ACOG not recommend internal iliac balloon catheters. (Book p459)

questions.q: Postnatally detected PAS presents with:
opts: Intractable PPH, placenta that cannot be separated (no plane of separation), and +/− hematuria from percreta bladder infiltration
Snowstorm USG with theca lutein cysts
questions.exp: Intractable PPH, absent separation plane and hematuria (percreta) mark postnatal PAS. (Book p459)

questions.q: Management of postnatally detected PAS is:
questions.exp: Emergency hysterectomy is the management. (Book p459)

questions.q: If fertility is desired in postnatal PAS, the conservative procedure includes:
opts: Placenta left in situ with cord ligated close to insertion, hysterotomy closed, plus compression sutures/tamponade packing
questions.exp: Conservative care leaves the placenta in situ, ligates the cord, closes the hysterotomy and uses compression sutures/packing. (Book p459)

questions.q: Follow-up investigations after conservative PAS management and the two interventions with NO role are:
opts: Serial USG/MRI; no role for serial β-hCG or injection methotrexate
Serial β-hCG; no role for USG
Serial MTX levels; no role for MRI
questions.exp: Serial USG/MRI follow the patient; serial β-hCG and methotrexate have no role. (Book p459)

questions.q: After conservative (fertility-sparing) management of PAS, what proportion ultimately require hysterectomy?
questions.exp: About 20% will ultimately need hysterectomy. (Book p459)

units.title: definition & causes → etiopathogenesis
units.guide: Define APH, rank its causes and contrast the painless bleeding mechanism of previa with the thromboplastin-driven cascade of abruptio. Focus for this checkpoint: APH: definition & causes, PP vs abruptio: etiopathogenesis.

units.title: important features & classification
units.guide: Learn why previa is diagnosed only in the third trimester and place types 1-3 of the old classification by placental edge position. Focus for this checkpoint: PP: important features & classification.

units.title: PP types & abruptio varieties
units.guide: Finish the old classification with type 4, apply the new low-lying/previa split and grade abruptio by the Page classification and clot/bleeding pattern. Focus for this checkpoint: PP types & abruptio varieties.

units.title: risk factors & associations
units.guide: Contrast recurrence rates and risk lists of previa and abruptio, and attach the named associations: Stallworthy sign, Couvelaire uterus, CAOS and precipitate labour. Focus for this checkpoint: PP vs abruptio: risk factors & associations.

units.title: presentation & examination
units.guide: Discriminate previa from abruptio on bleeding character, shock correspondence, abdominal findings and the contraindicated digital exam, then choose TVS as IOC. Focus for this checkpoint: PP vs abruptio: presentation & examination.

units.title: Management of placenta previa
units.guide: Run the third-trimester bleeding drill: two large cannulas, ABC, three assessment parameters and the instant C-section rule, ending with the Jello sign and migration rates. Focus for this checkpoint: Management of placenta previa.

units.title: follow-up & mode of delivery
units.guide: Follow a low-lying placenta through 32- and 36-week scans to the 36-37 week C-section plan and match delivery route to os distance. Focus for this checkpoint: PP: follow-up & mode of delivery.

units.title: expectant vs active management
units.guide: Apply the MacAfee/Johnson's regime criteria, steroid and tocolytic windows and the accreta suspicion that converts C-section into caesarean hysterectomy. Focus for this checkpoint: PP: expectant vs active management.

units.title: Management of abruptio & DIC → differential diagnosis
units.guide: Decide C-section versus vaginal delivery in abruptio by maternal and fetal state, treat consumptive coagulopathy and separate labour, abruptio and ruptured uterus at the bedside. Focus for this checkpoint: Management of abruptio & DIC, APH: differential diagnosis.

units.title: classification & etiopathogenesis → risk factors & investigations
units.guide: Grade the accreta spectrum by FIGO, explain the missing Nitabuch's layer and read the Doppler signs that make 28 weeks the diagnostic sweet spot. Focus for this checkpoint: PAS: classification & etiopathogenesis, PAS: risk factors & investigations.

units.title: management
units.guide: Plan the ACOG caesarean hysterectomy at 34-35 weeks, weigh ureteric and internal iliac catheters and manage postnatally detected accreta with or without fertility wishes. Focus for this checkpoint: PAS: management.
